standard_prerequisites.use: Chapter lemma quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite (the ZMT compactification); elementary facts on scheme-theoretic images of quasi-compact opens and closed immersions which are dense; finiteness of coproducts of finite S-schemes.

core_obligations: Compactify V to a finite S-scheme V' with dense image.
Prove no extra geometric points appear over U via the closed-and-dense argument.
Adjoin the boundary to achieve surjectivity without touching the restriction.
difficulty_reason: For S quasi-compact quasi-separated, U a quasi-compact open, and V -> U surjective finite, the lemma produces a surjective finite morphism Vbar -> S with Vbar x_S U isomorphic to V over U. The retained proof is written: Zariski's Main Theorem form (chapter lemma quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite, already collected) embeds V as a quasi-compact open of a scheme V' finite over S; replacing V' by the scheme-theoretic image of V makes V dense in V'; then V' x_S U = V because V -> V' x_S U is an open immersion finite over U hence closed with dense image, so surjective; finally Vbar = V' coproduct Z with Z the reduced induced structure on S \ U is finite surjective over S and restricts to V over U. Retained author proof at lines 13713-13723.

dedup.scope: Extension of surjective finite covers from qc opens of qcqs schemes.
